libraries.name: Apache ECharts
libraries.what_for: Configuration-driven charts of almost every standard type, with built-in interaction, animation, maps and large-data rendering on canvas.
libraries.note: Built from the gallery's own index files in apache/echarts-examples (src/data/chart-list-data.js and chart-list-data-gl.js on gh-pages), keeping the 282 core and 59 GL entries that have a title and category and lack the noExplore flag; the other 95 core entries are hidden from the gallery. ECharts GL (3D) examples have categories prefixed 'GL:' and need the echarts-gl extension.

libraries.name: D3.js
libraries.what_for: Low-level toolkit for binding data to SVG, canvas or HTML, giving full control over scales, layouts, geography, transitions and interaction.
libraries.note: Built from the source of the official Observable gallery notebook (api.observablehq.com/@d3/gallery.js). The 56 example notebooks linked from the d3js.org homepage all appear in this gallery. All 174 notebooks were confirmed to exist through the Observable API. A few entries are notebooks by Mike Bostock or others that the gallery links to.

libraries.name: globe.gl
libraries.what_for: Three.js-based 3D globe component for points, arcs, polygons, paths, hexbins, heatmaps and labels on a sphere.
libraries.note: Built from the Examples list in the README, which globe.gl renders as its homepage. The gallery has no categories. Each live example's source is in the repo's example/ folder.

libraries.name: deck.gl
libraries.what_for: GPU-powered WebGL layers for large geospatial and non-geospatial datasets: arcs, hexbins, heatmaps, trips, point clouds and tiles over base maps.
libraries.note: Built from the gallery sidebar (website/src/examples-sidebar.js on the 9.4-release branch, which matches the live site). Titles come from each example page's heading. Pages that are live but missing from the gallery sidebar (first-person-view, grid-layer, simple-mesh-layer) are left out, as is the PathStyleExtension example that exists only on master and is not deployed yet.

libraries.name: three.js
libraries.what_for: General-purpose 3D engine for WebGL and WebGPU: scenes, cameras, lights, materials, models, shaders and post-processing.
libraries.note: Built from the gallery's own index, threejs.org/examples/files.json, so the list is complete. Titles follow the gallery's display rule (file name minus its prefix, underscores as slashes).

libraries.name: Sigma.js
libraries.what_for: WebGL renderer for large node-link graphs on top of graphology, with fast pan, zoom, hover and custom node and edge programs.
libraries.note: Built from the storybook's index.json plus the full demo linked from the homepage. Demo source: https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js/tree/main/packages/demo.

examples.title: Customize how sigma handles sizes and positions
Node drag'n'drop, with mouse graph creation

libraries.name: Cytoscape.js
libraries.what_for: Graph theory library and renderer for network analysis and visualisation, with many layouts, compound nodes, a CSS-like style system and graph algorithms.
libraries.note: Built from the Demos section of js.cytoscape.org. Several demos belong to extensions and are hosted on the extension's own GitHub Pages site, linked from the official page.

libraries.name: Cosmograph
libraries.what_for: GPU force-directed layout and rendering for graphs and embeddings with hundreds of thousands to millions of points, plus timeline, histogram and legend widgets.
libraries.note: The library docs (cosmograph.app/docs-lib) have no example gallery, so this lists the showcase page's public Cosmograph projects plus the storybook of cosmos.gl, the open-source engine Cosmograph is built on (linked from the cosmograph-org/cosmos README).

libraries.name: Vega and Vega-Lite
libraries.what_for: Declarative JSON grammars of graphics: Vega-Lite for concise statistical charts with linked interaction, Vega for full control of marks, transforms and signals.
libraries.note: Built from docs/_data/examples.json in vega/vega and site/_data/examples.json in vega/vega-lite. Categories start with 'Vega:' (94 examples) or 'Vega-Lite:' (203 entries). The Vega-Lite gallery lists 14 examples under two sections each, so it holds 189 distinct examples; both listings are kept. Vega gallery: https://vega.github.io/vega/examples/.
